newsitem.title: CHINA: Shenzhen B shares lower at noon in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares lower at noon in slow trade.

text.p: Shenzhen's hard currency B share index edged lower at midday on Tuesday, with most investors relunctant to trade in the absence of fresh factors, brokers said.
The B share index lost 0.13 point or 0.10 percent to 130.75 on turnover of HK$14.5 million.
The domestic A share index advanced 1.71 points or 0.41 percent to 415.70 on turnover of 2.1 billion yuan.
"B share investment is still depressed," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said. "The market lacks buying interest."
Taiwan-invested appliance maker Tsann Kuen Ltd was the biggest B share loser, falling HK$0.15 or 4.84 percent to HK$2.95 on a tiny volume of 2,300 shares.
Television tube maker Shenzhen SEG, the market's big gainer on Monday, maintained its upward momentum, rising HK$0.31 or 5.86 percent to HK$5.60 on volume of 684,810 shares.
Brokers said SEG was targeted by some institutional bargain hunters after the issue's recent sharp falls.
"B shares are expected to trend up slowly, but sharp rises are unlikely in the near future," an analyst at J&A Securities (HK) said.
Bengang Steel Plates 2761.SZ remained unchanged at HK$2.13 on volume of 961,600 shares. It was the morning's most active B share issue.
On the A share market, nonferrous metals processor Zhuhai Shining was the best performer, gaining 0.53 yuan or 5.75 percent to 9.74 yuan on volume of 1.9 million shares.
